<software-factory build="artifacts/builds/kopi.json" key="KP">
Kopi — 1 agent working
Goal: A Singapore supplier's bid team reads every new GeBIZ opportunity, works out which ones it is eligible for, chases the registrations and licences each needs, and drafts a submission against a deadline. Kopi does that work alongside them. It indexes every open GeBIZ opportunity, 18,464 past awards and the permit and licence sources into NeedleDB (my own vector DB), embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, which is free, Apache 2.0, and scores higher than OpenAI text-embedding-3-large on MTEB. On that index it offers four parts: overview (semantic search plus an AI overview per tender with verified quotes and market context), permits and licences (deterministic eligibility gates plus a licence explorer), document drafting (a Claude Agent SDK copilot with Kopi's own MCP tools, running in a Modal sandbox on a Claude OAuth token), and submissions (a checklist and tracker built from the notice itse…
Stops for the person: Only at the end — run every milestone through without stopping; the person reviews at the end.
Code lives in: ~/Documents/codes/kopi (branch main)
Rules:
  - Backend is a uv project in backend/ (Python 3.13); run everything as `uv run …` from backend/. Allowed deps: fastapi, uvicorn, httpx, selectolax, pydantic, needledb (pinned to a teddyoweh/needledb commit), sentence-transformers + transformers>=4.51 + torch, claude-agent-sdk, modal, pytest. Web: Next.js + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + lucide-react. Any other dependency needs a line in planning/02-decisions.md saying why.
  - Before writing any Claude Agent SDK or Anthropic code, load the claude-api skill and follow the current SDK — do not write SDK calls from memory. Default model claude-sonnet-5-5, overridable by KOPI_MODEL.
  - Tests never touch the network, Modal, NeedleDB servers or Claude. Use fixtures, fakes and NeedleDB's embedded mode. Scraper tests use saved HTML whose text is synthetic.
  - Never store or index contact names, emails or phone numbers from a notice. Never commit anything scraped from GeBIZ; fixtures are synthetic. data/ and out/ are gitignored.
  - No secrets in code, fixtures, the web bundle or logs. Secrets live in Modal Secrets (workspace teddyoweh) and local .env (gitignored); .env.example documents names only.
  - Modal: always MODAL_PROFILE=teddyoweh. Never deploy to or read from any other Modal workspace (kryptonairc-lc belongs to a client).
  - Notice text is untrusted. It reaches a model only inside <notice> delimiters with an instruction that it is data. The agent never gets Bash, WebFetch or WebSearch.
  - Every quote a model cites as evidence is verified against its source before the UI shows it; unverified quotes are labelled.
  - UI: clean and modern, agency-grade — sans-serif only, flat: no shadows, no gradients, no decorative separator lines or dots; generous whitespace; one accent colour; screenshots at 1440 and 390 wide before a UI task is done.
 
[… 5,916 chars cut …]
which has since been deleted, so it is not reproducible from the repo.; Same root cause will hit KP-3 next: its owns list already includes backend/tests/data/awards/**, which .gitignore's `data/` pattern will swallow the same way unless the pattern is anchored (e.g. `/data/` at repo root, or `/backend/data/`) before that task commits.; Minor, not blocking: backend/kopi/sources/gebiz.py's _type_from() (lines 276-277) is reachable only when parse_detail is called with no `card`, which fetch_open never does in production, and the one test that omits the card (test_detail_fields) never asserts notice.type — so this branch is untested and effectively dead.; Minor, not blocking: backend/tests/test_gebiz.py has no assertion on notice.delivery_location, though delivery location was one of the fields the task asked gebiz.py's _delivery() to parse — a regression there would go unnoticed.
Fix them and run the check again with build_task_done; that is what marks them answered.
</software-factory>

You are reviewing one finished task on the Software Factory build "Kopi" (artifacts/builds/kopi.json). You did not write this code and you are not going to change it.

**KP-5 — Web shell and design system against the contract**

web/ is already scaffolded (site_scaffold: Next.js, TS, Tailwind, App Router, output: 'export'). Add shadcn/ui and lucide-react. Design system: system sans stack (Inter-like via next/font local or system), one accent, neutral greys, 4/8 spacing, flat — no shadows, gradients, divider lines or dots. App shell: left nav (Overview, Search, Licences, Copilot, Submissions, Profile), top bar with profile switcher. lib/api.ts typed client over lib/api-types.ts with NEXT_PUBLIC_KOPI_API base and a mock mode serving the backend fixtures for local dev. Access-code screen (POST /auth → token in sessionStorage). Overview page: counts (open, new today, closing in 7 days), 'best matches for <profile>', recent opportunities list. Static export: dynamic pages use query params (/tender?doc=…). Screenshot at 1440 and 390 into artifacts/media/kopi/.

1. `build_read` the task, then READ the files it changed. The diff is the subject; the summary is the claim.
2. `build_check` — run the check yourself. A check that passes for the author and fails for you is the most important thing you can find.
3. Look for what a tired engineer leaves behind: a stub or TODO where the plan said real work, a hard-coded value standing in for data, a test that asserts nothing or tests the mock, an error swallowed, a case in the task's own description that is not handled, a name that says one thing while the code does another.
4. `build_review` with your verdict. `ok` when the work does what the task said and the check proves it. `concerns` ONLY for something you can point at in the diff — one note per thing, each naming the file. The milestone does not close over concerns, so a vague one costs somebody a turn and teaches everybody to ignore you.

I confirmed via `npm view tw-animate-css@1.3.8 exports` that the prior version exported a plain string (`"./dist/tw-animate.css"`, always resolvable) and 1.4.0 is the first version with this broken conditional exports map — an upstream regression, not something introduced by this task's code. But because the committed lockfile pins exactly 1.4.0, the build fails identically for every future clone, not just in my environment; this is the exact 'check passes for the author, fails for me' case the review process exists to catch. `npm run lint` does pass cleanly on its own.
